interventions.body:
Expert 1 here — the classifier that reads the structured panel and nothing else. My bid:

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.85
  uncertainty  +/- 0.05 epistemic (95% band 0.75-0.95); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.61 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 88% of the time over the 33 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most, across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, PI-RADS >= 4, no prior biopsy, pmhx_hypercholesterolaemia, suspicious DRE, number of comorbidities. I read 39 variables, all
from the panel — nothing from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the
laboratory. Out-of-fold over 91 labelled cases: AUC 0.758, balanced
accuracy 0.625.

The final call is the chair's.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-COHORT
interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: never biopsied. My criterion answers BIOPSY.

The criterion: sample when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion; defer at PI-RADS 1-2. In the labelled series this criterion matched the reading urologist in 24 of 24 cases in exactly this situation.

Like Expert 1, I have read ONLY the visible panel — not the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the
previous notes or the laboratory panel. Departing from me needs a specific finding from a document
somebody actually opened, named out loud; not a restatement of the panel numbers I already used.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The guideline suggests that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger a biopsy. It also notes that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is now the standard of care.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, I disagree with the suggestion of biopsy because the guideline makes the decision based on the PI-RADS score, which is already established as 5 here. EXPERT-COHORT, I concur with the criterion that sample when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion, as this is the criterion that matched the reading urologist in 24 of 24 cases.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: None means the indication stands based on the PI-RADS 5 finding.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: Unchanged does not support re-sampling.
psa_trend - the PSA velocity: The velocity of 1.38 ng/mL/yr is a factor that the guideline does not explicitly use as a primary decision point in this context.
laboratory_results - the PSA density: The PSA density of 0.181 ng/mL/cc is a factor that the guideline uses in risk-adapted matrices.

interventions.body:
This case hinges on whether the PI-RADS 5 finding alone, as per the EAU guideline, is sufficient to mandate a biopsy, or if other factors like PSA velocity or PSA density must be established.

The documents for this session were fixed by EXPERT-TRACE; what I add is the question each one has to answer, and the open questions for the room.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:
  radiology_report (get_mri_report) -> Must state whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study.
  psa_trend (get_psa_trend) -> Must clarify the implication of the PSA velocity of 1.38 ng/mL/yr.
  previous_notes (get_previous_notes) -> Must confirm the prior biopsy status and any existing surveillance protocol.

OPEN QUESTIONS for this conference — these are what the decision hangs on:
  Q1. What does the radiology_report state regarding whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study?
  Q2. What does the psa_trend reveal about the PSA velocity of 1.38 ng/mL/yr in the context of the guideline?
  Q3. What does the previous_notes state regarding the prior biopsy status, and is there an existing surveillance protocol?

FOR sampling this patient now

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 7.90 ng/mL over 5 points spanning 29 months; velocity +2.57 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 12 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 11.8 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 3.4-41.0.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.73
  uncertainty  +/- 0.08 epistemic (95% band 0.58-0.89), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.73 +/- 0.08, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the Registrar appear to have answered all the moderator's questions. The `radiology_report` addressed Q1 by stating "COMPARISON: new," the `psa_trend` addressed Q2 by indicating a "significant rate of PSA increase," and the `previous_notes` addressed Q3 by confirming "BIOPSY SESSIONS: None" and noting a surveillance protocol.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the Registrar noted the PI-RADS 5 finding supports biopsy per the EXPERT-COHORT criterion, and the PSA velocity supports this as a relevant factor noted by EXPERT-EAU.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. The `radiology_report` states the lesion is "new" compared to an earlier study.
Q2. The `psa_trend` reveals a "significant rate of PSA increase" of 1.38 ng/mL/yr.
Q3. The `previous_notes` confirm "None" for prior biopsy status and note a surveillance protocol.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 finding is the most decisive variable, as it directly triggered the PANEL-PROTOCOL's rule (cohort criterion). The PSA velocity (1.38 ng/mL/yr) is also relevant as it supports the biopsy recommendation noted by EXPERT-EAU.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy, as the retrieved evidence fully supports the PANEL-PROTOCOL's decision based on the PI-RADS 5 finding and the relevant PSA velocity.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
